newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian condensate output rises to 180,000 bpd.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian condensate output rises to 180,000 bpd.

text.p: Nigeria's production of condensate has now risen to 180,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 150,000 bpd previously, a senior oil official said on Wednesday.

"The condensate production, when added to the nation's OPEC crude oil output quota, gives a total output of 2.04 million bpd," Chike Ozumba, head of the research and intelligence unit of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) told a workshop on energy data bank in Lagos.
Condensate, an extra-light hydracarbon, is not counted as part of its OPEC quota, which Nigeria has been accused of overshooting.
Ozumba said Nigeria had informed OPEC of its rising level of condensate production.
"We have even given indication that the level will reach 200,000 bpd when the NNPC/Mobil Oso II project comes on stream early next year," he added.
The Oso fields where condensate is produced is operated by the NNPC joint venture with Mobil Corp known as Mobil Nigeria Producing Unlimited.
